subject_property.property_identifier: Gadi Sirampur and four villages (Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna, Chihutia)

legal_framework: Transfer of Property Act (IV of 1882), ss. 66, 65-A
Act of 1929 (Amendment to Transfer of Property Act)

claims.issue: Does the Plaintiff (subrogated to Bank) hold a valid title and ownership interest in the subject property, and is the permanent lease granted by the mortgagor binding on the mortgagee?
claims.rule_and_authority: Under the law prior to s. 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act, a mortgagor in possession may make a lease conformable to usage in the ordinary course of management (e.g., tenancy from year to year for agricultural land). However, it is not competent to grant a lease of unusual terms or to alter the character of the land. The burden of proof is on the lessee to establish the lease was granted in the usual course of management.
elements: Source: Mortgage Decree vs Permanent Lease (Patta)
Breach / Cloud: Lease granted without concurrence of mortgagee and not in usual course of management
Harm: Loss of possession and title to Plaintiff
facts: Claimed property interest exists (Plaintiff purchased at auction).
Chain of title is documented (Mortgage -> Decree -> Sale -> Plaintiff).
Possession is disputed (Plaintiff seeks khas possession).
Competing title exists (Permanent Lease by Wazir Narain Singh).
Property records (Patta) exist but are alleged to be invalid against Plaintiff.

claims.issue: Is the Plaintiff entitled to recover khas possession from the Defendants who are in wrongful possession based on an invalid lease?
claims.rule_and_authority: If the lessee fails to establish that the lease was granted in the usual course of management, they have no defense against the mortgagee's claim for possession.
elements: Possessory Right: Actual possession by Defendants
Interference: Denial of Plaintiff's title and possession
Illegality: Lease not in usual course of management
Harm: Loss of possession and mesne profits
facts: Claimant is in possession (via Court of Wards).
Respondent has interfered (holding possession via lease).
Notice or due process is disputed (lease validity).
Possession is disputed (Plaintiff claims wrongful possession).
Urgent threat requiring interim protection exists (implied by suit for possession).
evidence: Court orders for delivery of possession

defenses_counter_narratives.defense_theory: Lease Validity / Ordinary Course of Management

possession_site_evidence: Court orders for delivery of possession

remedies_requested: Khas possession of the four villages (Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna, Chihutia)
Restoration of decree passed by trial court in favour of Plaintiff
Quashing of High Court decree dismissing Plaintiff's suit
missing_proof_evidentiary_gaps: Specific details on the 'usual course of management' for the specific villages in question to definitively prove or disprove the lease validity beyond the court's finding.
Detailed calculation of figures regarding the sufficiency of security as argued by the High Court (though Supreme Court found this irrelevant).
